descriptor.title: Which legal issues could derail this acquisition?
descriptor.introduction: What must we resolve before buying this startup? A fictional business decision with a reviewed action document.

strategies.title: Advice tested against business and legal risks
strategies.input_summary: Fictional Alder Systems proposes a $12 million acquisition of Delaware corporation Spruce Workflow. The term sheet says “stock acquisition or merger, structure to be agreed,” with a 30-day exclusivity period. The draft cap table omits two convertible notes. A founding contractor wrote the core scheduling engine before signing an assignment that names a different project. Spruce’s largest customer supplies 38% of recurring revenue; its contract has a change-of-control consent clause. A data-processing agreement limits customer data to service delivery. The financial model assumes immediate use of all target data to train Alder’s model. Two engineers are labeled contractors but work full time under management control. The term sheet is not a signed definitive acquisition agreement.
assumptions: All business facts and organizations in this scenario are fictional.
Missing facts must remain unresolved rather than assumed favorable.

revised.response_text:
## Recommendation
Do not treat the term sheet as closing authority. Resolve structure and approvals, reconcile fully diluted ownership, cure the core-IP chain and obtain or appropriately condition the major-customer consent before committing to the modeled valuation. Remove unrestricted data-training synergies from the base case unless contractual and legal authority is established.

## Risks
The acquisition structure determines what transfers, approvals, taxes and liabilities require analysis. Section 251 is a merger anchor, not clearance of every structure. Omitted convertible notes can alter consideration and consent needs. The defective project description may leave essential code ownership unresolved. Worker classification, data restrictions, competition review and other federal issues require separate facts and counsel; the $12 million headline price alone is not a universal exemption.

## Options
Proceed with a structure-specific definitive agreement containing evidence-based closing conditions and allocated risks. Reprice or defer consideration for unresolved IP/customer risks if commercially acceptable, recognizing that indemnity is only as useful as recovery. Exclude assets or data uses where a workable structure allows it. Walk away if title to essential code or the 38%-revenue customer relationship cannot be secured at an acceptable price.

## Next Steps
Corporate counsel: choose structure and map board, stockholder, noteholder and other required approvals. Finance: reconcile cap table, notes and consideration waterfall. IP counsel: inspect contribution history and obtain effective assignments from actual owners. Commercial/privacy teams: review consent and data-use terms. Employment and regulatory specialists: scope classification and transaction-specific federal review. Record each unresolved item in the investment committee’s decision.

## Secondary Deliverable
**Priority diligence request and draft closing conditions**
P0 ownership: charter, bylaws, securities ledger, all notes/options/warrants, approval records and a reconciled fully diluted waterfall.
P0 technology: contractor agreements, code contribution history, licenses and an executed assignment accurately covering the core engine from each necessary owner.
P0 revenue: largest-customer agreement, amendments and required written change-of-control consent or an approved structure-specific alternative.
P1 data/workforce: processing terms, data inventory, proposed post-close uses, worker duties, hours and agreements.
Draft condition concepts: evidence of required approvals for the chosen structure; agreed capitalization accuracy; satisfactory essential-IP title; required material-customer consent; no unsupported reliance on expanded data rights.
Proposed risk allocation: specific representations and indemnities or price adjustments for identified risks, with negotiated survival, caps, recovery source and disclosure schedules. These concepts require definitive drafting; none is satisfied by the term sheet alone.

## Source boundary
